_comment: claude.profiles.* is answered by the BRAIN for every web / mobile / remote /
MCP client (it is a catalog method) and by claudeProfiles.ts over IPC. The two
disagreed about what a profile store even contains:
list    the brain PREPENDED a synthetic {id:'default'} whenever no profile
carried isDefault, without ever writing it — two profiles there, one
here, for the same file; and it normalized extraArgs/mcpItemIds to []
while the desktop returned the file verbatim.
update  the brain then refused the very id it had just listed, because update
reads the raw file: `profile "default" not found`.
add     on a fresh config dir the brain minted isDefault:TRUE and the desktop
isDefault:FALSE, because the desktop's constructor had already
persisted the real Default row. This method carries `configDir`,
which becomes CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.
The convergent rule: MATERIALIZE the Default row (write it) when the store is
empty, normalize the list fields on read, and make list / add / update / remove
all operate on that one set.
`file` is claude-profiles.json's `profiles` array, or null for no file at all.
`<added>` in expectedFileIds stands for the freshly minted uuid.
THE BLOCK REGISTRY. Every array-of-objects block in this file must be declared
here and everything here must be a block — closure in both directions, so a new
block is a failure until someone says what its cases must carry, and a renamed
one cannot quietly stop being validated.
Held by cmd/brain/corpusvocab_test.go and
apps/desktop/src/main/services/contractsVocabulary.test.ts. Before those, this
kind of validation existed for exactly ONE block of ONE fixture.

list.why: loadProfiles over a seeded profiles file, and what it leaves on disk.

add.why: addProfile's answer and the id order it leaves behind.

mutate.why: update/remove against an id the caller got from list().

list.name: an absent profiles file materializes exactly one Default row
list.why: Both copies must WRITE the row, not merely pretend it is there. The brain prepended a synthetic {id:'default'} it never persisted, so claude.profiles.list returned an id that claude.profiles.update then answered `profile "default" not found` for.

list.name: an empty profiles array materializes the same Default row
list.why: Same state spelled differently on disk; a reader that only handled the missing-file case would diverge on a file written and then emptied.

list.name: an existing profile is listed as itself, normalized, with no phantom row
list.why: The divergence in one case: the brain returned TWO profiles (a synthetic Default plus p1) where the desktop returned ONE. Missing list fields normalize to [] on both sides — the brain has always served `mcpItemIds: []` and the desktop served the file verbatim, so the same profile came back with and without the key.

list.name: a profile that already carries the lists keeps them
list.why: The floor: normalization must not overwrite real values, and a populated file must not be rewritten.

add.name: add on a fresh config dir is NOT the default
add.why: The brain minted isDefault:TRUE (its readProfilesFile saw an empty file, because its Default was synthetic) and the desktop minted FALSE (its constructor had already persisted the Default). claude.profiles.add is bus-reachable and carries configDir, which becomes CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

add.name: add trims configDir and defaults the lists
add.why: `mcpItemIds ?? []` and the trim are both shared rules; a nil list marshals as JSON null in Go and clients index it as an array.

mutate.name: every id the list returns can be updated
mutate.why: The brain LISTED 'default' and then refused to update it, because list read a synthetic row and update read the raw file. A listed id that cannot be addressed is not a profile.

mutate.name: removing the Default profile is a no-op on both providers
mutate.why: claudeProfiles.ts: `if (id === 'default') return`. The rule has to hold wherever the row came from.
